assemble_backlog.description: Turns the epic/story files the Story Writers wrote into one backlog: backlog.md (the deliverable), backlog.csv (Jira import), backlog.json and a coverage report, plus build-order.md, data-model.md, schema.json, api.md, openapi.json, integrations.md and screens.md. Pure code, no AI: every story is checked against the EARS/Gherkin writing rules, every coverage item is checked against the stories that claim it, and nothing is silently dropped. Needs an earlier step that plans the hierarchy (build/backlog-plan.json, build/story-tasks.json) and writer steps that write one file per epic slice (stories/<task id>.json).
assemble_backlog.process: Checks every story against the EARS and Gherkin rules and every coverage item against the stories that claim it, orders the epics and stories by what each needs first, then writes the backlog, build-order.md and the companion documents. Once build/review.json exists it also packages Backlog.pdf and Backlog.zip, and lists any coverage item no story covers in gaps.md.

assemble_prototype.description: Stitches the screen pages the builder agents wrote into one clickable prototype. Pure code, no AI: every screen is included, links between screens work, and a coverage report lists anything missing. Needs an earlier step that lists the screens (build/screens.json) and a builder step that writes one page per screen (parts/).
assemble_prototype.process: Pours every screen's part into the fixed shell as one clickable prototype, then checks ids, links and expected transitions. With a design template it adds the template's CSS and, when the template has one, its own page frame. A screen with no usable part becomes a stub; below the coverage threshold the step fails, naming what is missing.

extract_prototype_ui.description: Reads the look and feel of the prototype a workflow is written against — a chained prototype_v2 run's prototype.html, or an uploaded HTML — by rendering it in a headless browser. Writes build/ui/: the effective design tokens (palette by usage, fonts, type scale, radii, shadows, brand colour), one screenshot per component kind, one screenshot per screen and the navigation between screens.

file_extract.description: Extract text from an uploaded file: extract_text / file_info / file_find / file_page_image (spec 019). ONE entry point for every type — a plain-text file (.txt, .md, .csv, .json) comes back as text in the tool result; a .pdf, .docx, .xlsx or .pptx is materialised into .extract/{format}/{name}/ (Office files converted by LibreOffice first) and the receipt names document.md to read; a .html or .htm is opened in a headless browser and materialised screen by screen into .extract/html/{name}/, falling back to a static read when no browser can launch (spec 021); anything else is refused in readable text. Page images are crops of the RENDERED page, so annotation arrows drawn over a screenshot survive where embedded-image extraction loses them.or PowerPoint document: extract_text / file_info / file_find / file_page_image (spec 019). One entry point for every format — an Office file is converted to PDF underneath and the caller never sees it. Materialises the document into layout-aware text with @[[image-N.png]] placeholders in reading order, where each image is a crop of the rendered page (preserving annotation arrows), not the embedded image.
